text:
noah_head_marketing: Heads up  we need a compact battlecard + an SDR routing cheat sheet for next week's webinar. Opponents: big cloud managed endpoints, single-API LLM vendors, and niche infra runtimes. Priority: rebut library for inbound queries + 2 quick social hooks. Keep it operational, not academic.
tess_field_engage: Agree. Field needs 3 quick plays: pricing, latency, compliance. One-liners + 1 supporting artifact each (graph, quote, doc link).
omar_data_ops: I can supply a cost-per-1k-tokens calc and a p95/p99 latency snapshot for our dedicated pool vs a generic cloud endpoint. Will generate a tiny table and a PNG for the battlecard. Need which model configs?
riley_content: Two social hooks drafted: (A) "Serving matters: predictability beats model hoarding  join our webinar to see live failover and real unit economics" (B) "When endpoints wobble, routing keeps UX steady  live demo + benchmarks inside". Will write short/long versions.
jen_legal: Quick reminder: no absolute "cheaper" claims without supporting data. Also avoid implying feature parity for managed services; you can say API surface parity for inference calls if we include nuance line.
bench_bot: bench-runner: job 1292 started on ci-ops-2. Payload: chat sim (avg ctx 800, gen 256), embed sim (512 tokens). Will post results to /docs/bench/1292 and attach png.
noah_head_marketing: Good. Tess  can you sketch the SDR routing flows? We want: if buyer says "we care about latency" -> show p99 graph + demo routing; if buyer says "we need on-prem" -> show private deployment parity + security checklist; if buyer says "we use cloud X" -> show multi-region/fallback play. Keep each play <=2 sentences.
tess_field_engage: Draft plays: 
- Latency: "We show your p99 under load + automatic model fallbacks; this keeps tail latency predictable even when an upstream model degrades."
- On-prem: "Same inference API surface available in VPC/on-prem; ops controls and KMS/HSM integrations let you meet audits."
- Cloud lock-in: "We route to regional variants and offer pinned model versions so migrations are low-risk; routing policies let you prioritize cost vs latency."
omar_data_ops: Pushed preliminary numbers: hosted endpoint (cloud-x) p95=210ms p99=480ms cost/1k= $2.10; redwood-dedicated p95=120ms p99=190ms cost/1k= $1.35. Notes: batch sizes differ; see /docs/bench/1292 for raw. PNG uploaded: /docs/bench/1292/p99-compare.png
riley_content: Nice numbers. I'll build a small inset for battlecard: "realized cost and tail latency comparison (chat workload)". Also writing 3 rebut bullets for SDRs: 
```
- "Predictable unit economics: we tune autoscaling + batching per-workload so realized token costs are lower under steady state."
- "Deterministic SLOs: routing + automatic fallbacks keep p99 stable during noisy neighbors or regional outages."
- "Operational parity: same API and observability available in VPC/on-prem; managed service differences are documented."
```
noah_head_marketing: Those rebut bullets look usable. Omar  add a 1-paragraph "methodology" we can paste into the card that explains batch sizes, runner types, and what the numbers don't claim (e.g., not an apples-to-apples across custom infra).
jen_legal: Approve the methodology inclusion as long as it contains the caveat you just mentioned. Also please add: "Benchmarks performed with internal configs; results may vary for customer workloads."
omar_data_ops: Added methodology: "chat sim: 800 context avg, 256 gen; batch sizes tested [1,8,32]; runs on dedicated GPU pools vs standard cloud-managed endpoint. Costs calculated using token accounting and internal price-rate tables. These results illustrate trend, not certified SLA." Posted /docs/bench/1292/methodology.md
tess_field_engage: I'll format a 1-pager SDR cheat sheet and drop it in the playbook. Will include 2 pull quotes, the p99 graph, and the three plays. ETA: later today.
riley_content: Also created two webinar CTAs for landing page: short: "See predictable inference economics in action  join our webinar"; long: "Join our engineering leads to learn how serving, routing, and caching reduce real-world inference costs and keep latency predictable. Live demo + Q&A."
bench_bot: bench-runner: job 1292 completed. Result: artefacts uploaded to /docs/bench/1292. Summary: dedicated beats hosted on p99 and cost in our config.
noah_head_marketing: Awesome. Next steps: tess -> SDR 1-pager; riley -> social + landing copy + battlecard draft; omar -> final PNG + methodology link in card; jen -> final legal signoff. We meet again tomorrow 10:30 to bake final wording. Any blockers?
jen_legal: No blockers pending review.
noah_head_marketing: Ok closing thread. Drop assets in the doc: https://redwood-internal/marketing/playbooks/inference-launch and ping when complete. :rocket:
